stops.title: Orbital magnetic moment & Bohr magneton
stops.inShort: An electron revolving in an orbit of radius r with speed v produces orbital magnetic moment m_orb = evr/2 = (e/2m_e) L. Minimum orbital magnetic moment for n = 1 in hydrogen atom is Bohr magneton μ_B = eh / (4π m_e) = 9.274 × 10⁻²⁴ A·m².

stops.title: Magnetization, magnetic intensity & susceptibility
stops.inShort: Magnetization M = m_net / V (A/m). Magnetic intensity H = B₀/μ₀. In a material: B = μ₀(H + M). Magnetic susceptibility χ = M/H; relative permeability μ_r = 1 + χ.

stops.title: Dia-, Para- and Ferromagnetism, Curie's law & Hysteresis
stops.inShort: Diamagnetic (χ < 0, weakly repelled), Paramagnetic (χ > 0 small, obeys Curie's law χ = C/T), Ferromagnetic (χ >> 0, domains, loses ferromagnetism above Curie temperature T_c). Hysteresis loop area represents energy loss per unit volume per cycle; retentivity is B when H = 0.

items.s: Magnetic moment of electron in 1st Bohr orbit.

items.f: B = μ₀(H + M),  χ = M/H,  μ_r = 1 + χ

items.s: For paramagnetic materials; C is Curie constant.

board.text: What is value of B called, when H = 0 is in the hysteresis loop?
board.answer: Retentivity (or remanence) — the magnetic induction B remaining in the ferromagnetic specimen when the magnetizing field H is reduced to zero.

board.text: Write the mathematical formula for Bohr magneton for an electron revolving in nth orbital.
board.answer: μ_n = n e h / (4π m_e), and for n = 1 (Bohr magneton): μ_B = e h / (4π m_e).

board.text: Distinguish between diamagnetic, paramagnetic and ferromagnetic substances (any three points).
board.answer:
1. Susceptibility χ: small negative for diamagnetic; small positive for paramagnetic; very large positive for ferromagnetic.
2. Relative permeability μ_r: slightly less than 1 (diamagnetic); slightly greater than 1 (paramagnetic); much greater than 1 (ferromagnetic).
3. In non-uniform magnetic field: weakly repelled (diamagnetic); weakly attracted (paramagnetic); strongly attracted (ferromagnetic).
